title: URL State — Search Params and Shareable UI State

subChunks.title: URL State — Search Params and Shareable UI State
subChunks.hookHtml: Not all state belongs in React. Filter settings, search queries, pagination, sort order, and active tabs are all UI state that users expect to survive a page refresh and be shareable via a link. Put this state in the URL. When a user shares /quests?filter=active&sort=xp&page=2, the recipient sees the exact same view.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Why URL state matters

React state is ephemeral — it resets on refresh. URL state is persistent and shareable. Any UI state that represents a 'view' — what the user is looking at — belongs in the URL:

  • Search query
  • Active filter
  • Sort order
  • Pagination (current page)
  • Active tab
  • Modal open state (sometimes)

State that belongs in React: form field values being typed (not yet submitted), UI toggle states that don't represent navigation.

React Router's useSearchParams

import { useSearchParams } from 'react-router-dom';

function QuestBoard() {
  const [searchParams, setSearchParams] = useSearchParams();

  // Read:
  const filter = searchParams.get('filter') || 'all';
  const sort   = searchParams.get('sort') || 'name';
  const page   = parseInt(searchParams.get('page') || '1', 10);

  // Write — updates the URL without a page reload:
  function handleFilterChange(newFilter) {
    setSearchParams(prev => {
      prev.set('filter', newFilter);
      return prev;
    });
  }

  function handleSortChange(newSort) {
    setSearchParams(prev => {
      prev.set('sort', newSort);
      prev.set('page', '1'); // Reset to page 1 when sort changes
      return prev;
    });
  }
}

Reading params with defaults

// searchParams.get() returns null if the param doesn't exist:
const filter = searchParams.get('filter') ?? 'all';
const page   = Number(searchParams.get('page') ?? 1);

// Create a helper for typed access:
function getParam(params, key, defaultVal) {
  return params.get(key) ?? defaultVal;
}

Preserving params when navigating

import { Link, useSearchParams } from 'react-router-dom';

function Pagination({ totalPages }) {
  const [searchParams] = useSearchParams();

  function buildPageLink(pageNum) {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams);
    params.set('page', pageNum.toString());
    return `?${params.toString()}`;
  }

  return (
    <div>
      {Array.from({ length: totalPages }, (_, i) => (
        <Link key={i + 1} to={buildPageLink(i + 1)}>{i + 1}</Link>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

Vex: "Ask yourself: if a user pastes this URL to a colleague, should the colleague see the same thing? If yes, that state belongs in the URL. If the answer is 'no, the state is just local UI animation or a temporary form value', it belongs in React state."

storyBeats.text: An apprentice filters the quest board to show only fire-magic quests, sorted by difficulty. They copy the URL and send it to their partner. The partner opens it and sees the exact same filtered view. 'The URL is the state,' says Vex.

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: Search params are the most underused React Router feature. They give you persistent, shareable state for free. Filters, sort orders, pagination — all the things users want to bookmark and share. The URL is the best state container for view configuration.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a <FilteredQuestBoard /> using URL search params:

  • Two filter buttons: 'All' and 'Active' — update ?filter= in the URL
  • A text input for search — updates ?q= in the URL
  • Filter and search quests based on URL params
  • Show <p data-testid="filter-value"> with current filter value and <p data-testid="search-value"> with current search query

guidedPracticeTests.label: Typing in search updates search value

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a paginated list from scratch with full URL state. Page, page size (10/25/50), and a search query all live in search params. Navigating to a URL with params pre-populates the UI. Changing any control updates the URL. Include a 'Copy link' button that copies the current URL to clipboard.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the decision of 'URL state vs React state'. Give three examples of state that belongs in the URL and three examples that belong in React. What user experience breaks if you put filter/sort state in React instead of the URL?

questions.prompt: Which React Router hook is used to read and update URL search params?
options: useSearchParams — returns [searchParams, setSearchParams] similar to useState
useParams — reads dynamic route segments like :id
useLocation — returns the full URL location object
useURLState — a custom hook you must build yourself
questions.answer: useSearchParams — returns [searchParams, setSearchParams] similar to useState
questions.explanation: useSearchParams works like useState but for the URL's query string. searchParams is a URLSearchParams object (with .get(), .set(), .delete()), and setSearchParams updates the URL without a page reload.

questions.prompt: A user filters a product list to show only 'in stock' items, then refreshes the page. The filter resets. What is the fix?
options: Store the filter in URL search params — the value persists across refreshes and is shareable
Store the filter in localStorage and read it on mount
Use React Context so the filter survives remounts
questions.answer: Store the filter in URL search params — the value persists across refreshes and is shareable
questions.explanation: URL state persists across refreshes (it's in the URL) and is shareable — the user can send the link and the recipient sees the same filtered view. localStorage works for persistence but the state isn't reflected in the URL, so links aren't shareable. Context resets on page reload.

questions.prompt: A form has a 'country' dropdown that auto-populates city options. Should the country selection live in URL params or React state?
options: React state — it's an intermediate form selection that doesn't represent a shareable view; the user isn't 'navigating to' a country filter
URL params — all form values that affect UI should be in the URL
URL params — country is a filter that affects what options appear
Neither — use a ref to track the selected country
questions.answer: React state — it's an intermediate form selection that doesn't represent a shareable view; the user isn't 'navigating to' a country filter
questions.explanation: URL state is for view configuration that users want to share or bookmark — search queries, active filters, pagination, sort order. An in-progress form is temporary input the user is working through. Putting form fields in the URL exposes sensitive data, pollutes browser history, and confuses users.
